title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is explaining Lagrange's device (Misc. Taurinensia, c. 1766–69) for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y. Introduce an auxiliary time t with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y. Differentiating gives 2 d²x/dt² = X′ and 2 d²y/dt² = Y′. In §§27–30 he used p = x+y and treated the quadratic case X = A+Bx+Cx².

§31 gives a second route via q = x−y. Then 2 q″ = X′ − Y′. For the general quartic X = A+Bx+Cx²+Dx³+Ex⁴ one has X′ − Y′ = 2Cq + 3Dq(x+y) + 4Eq(x²+xy+y²). Only if D = E = 0 is the right side a function of q alone, namely q″ = Cq. Multiplying by 2dq and integrating gives (dq/dt)² = Const + Cq², so dq/dt = √(Δ + Cq²).

§32: since dq/dt = √X − √Y, the algebraic integral is √X − √Y = √(Δ + C(x−y)²). Squaring:
- 2A + B(x+y) + C(x²+y²) − 2√(XY) = Δ + C(x−y)², i.e.
- 2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy − 2√(XY) = Δ, hence
- 2√(XY) = (2A−Δ) + B(x+y) + 2Cxy.

The §29 integral gives 2√(XY) = Γ + B(x+y) + 2Cxy with Γ = Δ−2A. So the two integrals coincide after renaming the arbitrary constant.

§33: for the 'sum' equation dx/√X + dy/√Y = 0, replace √Y by −√Y in the earlier integrals. This gives √X − √Y = √(Δ + 2B(x+y) + C(x+y)²) and (next page) √X + √Y = √(Δ + C(x−y)²).

Purpose: these are pedagogical preliminaries for the quartic case, where Euler shows that Lagrange's method reproduces his own canonical symmetric biquadratic integral α + 2β(x+y) + γ(x²+y²) + 2δxy + … = 0, i.e. the addition theorem.
errors: Printed '2ddq/dt' should be 2 ddq/dt² (and likewise 2ddp/dt² in the parallel passage).
Printed 'X′ − X′ = 2Cq + 3Dq(x+y)' should read X′ − Y′. The full expression also contains the term 4Eq(xx+xy+yy), which the text omits even while stating that E = 0 is required.

The identification '2A − Δ = −Γ' is a sign inconsistency relative to §29, where Δ − 2A = Γ gives 2√XY = Γ + B(x+y) + 2Cxy. Here the natural choice is 2A − Δ = Γ. The discrepancy is harmless because the constant is arbitrary.
In §33 the first radicand appears printed as A + Bxx + Cxx; it should be A + Bx + Cxx (typographical).

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary parameter t with dx/dt = √X, dy/dt = √Y and working with x−y to get a second-order ODE integrable by multiplying by dq.
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's mechanical/dynamical method for the Euler addition theorem (energy-integral trick)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Misc. Taurinensia IV, 1766–69); expounded by Euler in E506
ideas.where_published: E506, Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778:I (publ. 1780)

ideas.what: Showing that the q = x−y route gives the same algebraic integral as the p = x+y route (up to renaming the constant), and the sign switch √Y → −√Y for the sum equation.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of first integrals / symmetric addition relation for quadratic radicals
ideas.where_published: E506; cf. E251, E252, Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 1

deep.surprise_reason: A routine expository verification within a well-known paper on Lagrange's method. Nothing here is new or uncredited; the only items of note are minor misprints.
transcription_corrections: '2ddq/dt' → '2ddq/dt²' (the image itself seems to show dt; the intended reading is dt²).
'X′ − X′' is faithful to the print but is an error for X′ − Y′.
In §32 the image reads '2A − Δ = −Γ' (a Greek Gamma), not 'F'.
In §33 the '[?]' between the fractions is '+'; the first radicand in the image reads approximately 'A + B.xx + C.xx'.
